runs.name: Companhia Paranaense de Energia - COPEL; NYSE ELPC ADSs of four common shares, B3 CPLE3, SEC CIK 0001041792, 20-F filer in Brazilian reais under IFRS; the largest energy company in Parana: hydro and wind generation, transmission, distribution to about 5.28 million customers and free-market trading; state control ended August 2023, Compagas and UEG Araucaria disposed of 2024, Baixo Iguacu and small hydro sold, Novo Mercado migration December 2025 (preferred shares and ADSs exchanged for common), Latibex delisting announced 2026-09-17; the 20-F's competition section names no company, AXIA and CEMIG chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **R$ 17.70** (CPLE3 B3 close 2026-10-16; ELPC US$ 13.97 NYSE, about R$ 71.0 an ADS at PTAX R$ 5.0826 of 2026-10-16, Banco Central do Brasil; aggregator, flagged). Shares **2,970,070,324** common outstanding (2,982,810,590 on the 20-F cover less 12,740,266 treasury, note 27.1 and Item 16E; `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing on the cover; the State's one special-class golden share not added), ADS = four shares; market cap R$ 52,570M. Sovereign **12.87%**, NTN-F 2037 buying rate of 2026-10-15 from the Tesouro Nacional's own file `PrecoTaxaTesouroDireto.csv` (the series a CONVENTION of the run, the protocol's table covering USD, JPY and EUR only). Read from the 20-F FY2025 (0002070979-26-000155), the 20-Fs FY2024, FY2023, FY2022, FY2020, FY2018 and FY2016, the 2Q26 results release on 6-K (0001292814-26-004089) and the 6-Ks of 2026-07-16 on the dividend policy; no proxy, Items 6 and 7 stand for it; no 2Q26 interim statements found on EDGAR; lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 4, 3.D and 5, stated in the run file; FY2024 operating cash R$ 3,394M and equity R$ 25,637M cross-checked to the filed statements; `tools/run.py` UNRESEARCHED on the IFRS 20-F, every figure from the filed statements. **Q1 IN**: four parts, generation, transmission, distribution and trading, each on stated contracts, tariff formulas and concession terms; no controller since 2023, a 10% vote cap; a commodity price not a Q1 stop, Brazil asking a lower price, not a pass. **Q2 OUT**: no part over half of 2021 to 2025 operating profit (generation 42.1%, distribution 30.7%, transmission 25.6%, trading 1.6%), so the largest, generation, decides (GET read whole also gives generation, 62% of it); a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns: the dams cannot be duplicated, but every concession is re-tendered or re-priced by the grantor at expiry, COPEL paying a R$ 4,074M grant bonus in November 2024 to keep Foz do Areia, Segredo and Salto Caxias to 2054, the 2025 sector laws setting renewals at the concession's estimated value with the hydrological risk on the operator, AXIA's 2022 renewals the same pattern; the energy sold at the market's price, wind curtailment 15.7% to 23.7% from 2Q25 to 2Q26; the field's return on equity about the long bond or below over ten years (COPEL 11.7% 2016 to 2025, AXIA 7.8%, CEMIG 17.5% with disposal gains and tax credits it names, the NTN-F average 10.9%); not TOO HARD. Q3 to Q12 not reached. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: the 2Q26 release leads with "Recurring" EBITDA and net income (here below reported); Executive Board pay R$ 10.0M (2023) to R$ 40.3M and R$ 41.9M after state control ended; performance shares vest on total shareholder return; buybacks of December 2024 and January 2025 at about R$ 8.3 to R$ 9.4 named no price and sit above the bottom of every computed case; no guidance search made. Debt R$ 23,484M with swaps, net R$ 19,651M at 2026-06-30, no dollar debt, CDI- and IPCA-indexed, pre-tax coverage about 2.6x in 2025. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE, all-equity central (the analyst decided from the filing that Q7, The regulated utility, does not make equity-only central because the deciding part, generation, is market-priced; equity-only beside, the utility debt credit shown as a third figure): owner cash **R$ 2,394M a year** all-equity maintenance-only (2021 to 2025, continuing operations, depreciation as the maintenance guess, interest added back after 34% tax, the 2021 CRC transfer to the State removed, the 2024 grant bonus spread over 30 years as a CONVENTION of the run), R$ 1,462M equity-only maintenance-only, R$ 401M equity-only after all spending (R$ -278M with the bonus charged in full); growth by (b)'s halves, all-equity cut by (f) from 16.9% to the 5.6% sales growth, the 2022 to 2025 decline beside; value range **R$ -0.35 to R$ 2.31 a share all-equity** (R$ 3.82 to R$ 7.95 equity-only); fair price **R$ 3.35 a share all-equity, R$ 13.40 an ADS (US$ 2.64)**, R$ 7.90 a share equity-only (US$ 6.22 an ADS); no case earns the floor, the best about 6.7% at the price, below the floor and the bond. Balance sheets 2015 to 2025: debt up 2.6 times (R$ 7.8bn to R$ 20.0bn), equity 1.6 times including R$ 2.0bn of new shares in 2023, equity down in 2025 as dividends and the Novo Mercado premium exceeded net income; intangibles up R$ 8bn, the bonus included; receivables steady to falling against sales. Competitors: none named in the competition section; AXIA (20-F FY2025, 0001439124-26-000013) and CEMIG, the SEC filers named among the industry's participants, chosen as a CONVENTION; CELESC and Neoenergia named and not SEC filers, flagged; rivals before 2025 from XBRL tags, one year each cross-checked. Strongest evidence against: the grantor sells the dams back at their value at each renewal; the filer's own levered return on equity at or below its government's bond; owner cash after all spending about 0.8% of market value. Commits a6ed879c (template), a48c8b9f (Step 0, balance sheets, Q1), 371a536c (Q2), 3c51c8f3 (box, after the stop, computation, self-audit, gaps). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared: a `Test Runs/` listing filtered to 2026-10-18 showing other runs' names, among them the AXIAY run (not opened; AXIA used only through its own 20-F), CMS commit subjects in the session context and memory-index lines on the queue state, none used. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 51 ids, 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 32 adjacent quoted fragments, 7 flagged and all read: filing quotes (Item 4, Item 3.D, the 2Q26 release, AXIA's 20-F, a balance-sheet line) beside an id the sentence cites for its own point, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the floor below the sovereign: in BRL the bond (12.87%) is above the ten percent floor, so a price could clear the floor and lose to the bond, and Q7 is silent; (2) (a) and (b) collide when the window starts in a drought trough, the halves rate crediting the recovery while the later years decline; (3) the regulated-utility paragraph's deciding part when the filer's segment mixes a regulated part with a market-priced one; (4) no rule for a once-in-thirty-years concession renewal payment; (5) whether the all-equity add-back removes the interest tax shield; (6) the named-rival rule for a foreign filer whose competition section names no company. Could not get: 2Q26 interim financial statements; trade receivables 2015 to 2017; generation's own capital base (approximated from GET); a guidance search. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Companhia Paranaense de Energia - COPEL, ELPC; Parana generation, transmission, distribution and trading, a 20-F filer in reais; Q1 IN; Q2 OUT: generation decides at 42.1% of five-year operating profit, a standing castle protecting only ordinary returns, the grantor re-pricing the concessions at renewal (R$ 4,074M bonus of 2024 to keep the three big dams to 2054), the energy at market prices, the field's return on equity about the long bond or below; integrity facts recorded, not judged; computation only: owner cash R$ 2,394M a year all-equity maintenance-only, value range R$ -0.35 to R$ 2.31 a share vs R$ 17.70, fair R$ 3.35 all-equity (R$ 13.40 an ADS), R$ 7.90 equity-only; no case earns the floor; no citation slip; not held; not armed; framework gaps for the operator: the floor below a higher sovereign, (a) against (b) on a trough start, the deciding part in a mixed segment, a concession renewal payment, the interest tax shield in the all-equity add-back, the named-rival rule for a foreign filer)
